title: Made to Stick: Why Some Ideas Survive and Others Die
author: Chip Heath and Dan Heath
target_audience: Anyone seeking to make their ideas more memorable and impactful
core_themes: Why certain ideas 'stick' in memory and spread while others fade
The characteristics of memorable, impactful communication
The psychology of attention and understanding
Strategies for crafting simple, powerful messages
primary_purpose: To analyze and reveal the key principles that make ideas memorable, influential, and easily understood, providing practical frameworks to help readers communicate more effectively and ensure their messages are remembered and acted upon.

structure_format.organization: Structured around the SUCCES(s) framework—six principles that make ideas 'stick': Simplicity, Unexpectedness, Concreteness, Credibility, Emotions, Stories
features: Case studies and vivid real-life examples

key_concepts_lessons: Sticky ideas share six qualities: Simplicity, Unexpectedness, Concreteness, Credibility, Emotions, Stories (SUCCESs).
Stripping ideas to their core essence makes them easier to understand and remember.
Surprise and curiosity grab attention and help ideas stand out.
Concrete details make abstract concepts tangible and easier to recall.
Using credible sources and details establishes trust and believability.
Appealing to emotions helps people care about ideas, not just understand them.
Stories are a powerful vehicle for teaching, persuading, and inspiring action.
notable_features: Introduction of the SUCCES(s) framework for memorable communication
Extensive use of entertaining anecdotes and case studies
Well-researched, drawing insights from psychology, sociology, and business
Practical tips for immediate application in professional and personal contexts
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2000s at a time when viral ideas, marketing messages, and organizational change communication were increasingly critical in both business and civic spheres. The book builds on research from psychology and behavioral economics to bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world communication challenges.
reception_impact: Bestseller, translated into dozens of languages
Widely recommended by business leaders, educators, and communication experts
Credited as a modern classic on effective messaging and idea diffusion
Influential in the fields of education, nonprofit advocacy, and corporate communication
Praised for its readable style and actionable framework

The Tipping Point: How Little Things Can Make a Big Difference by Malcolm Gladwell
